key_insight: Woven Lundgren turbulence links three regions of the velocity-gradient Q–R distribution to distinct physics: stretching shapes the head, spiral vortex arms shape the body, and dissipation shapes the tail.
engineering_relevance: This physically interpretable framework could inform synthetic turbulence generation and statistical model assessment for turbulent-flow simulations.
method: Construct synthetic turbulence from an ensemble of Lundgren spiral vortices.
Vary background strain rate, vortex cutoff age, and viscous decay to track changes in P(Q,R).
Build an explicit P(Q,R) model combining stretching, spiral, and dissipation contributions.
evidence_signal: Parameter sweeps link stronger strain to a broader head, older vortex cutoffs to greater body inclination, and reduced viscous factors to a longer tail; the explicit model is validated against WLT statistics.
watch_item: The abstract reports validation against WLT statistics but does not establish quantitative accuracy for wall-bounded or anisotropic turbulence.
paper_title: Modelling velocity gradient invariants in turbulence with Lundgren spiral vortex ensemble
